messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV2 alert: sudden sustained KV cache size growth on shard-pool-7. Streaming token throughput on /v1/stream is spiking latency and causing partial flush backpressure. Auto-escalation to #incidents triggered.

oncall-ryan: Joining. stacking context: high evictions, memory climb on kvcached. Give me current P95/P99 for streaming and 5xx rates.

sre-amy: P95 streaming latency up from 120ms -> 520ms last 5m. P99 ~1.8s. 5xx rate for streaming up 0.9% -> 4.8%. KV cache hit ratio dropped from 91% -> 58%. ETA on root cause unknown.

eng-runtime-eric: Seeing continuous-batching queues grow. There's an odd pattern where batch size multiplier jumps to 64 for requests with prefix hits==0 causing huge GC and cache churn. Possibly a regression from yesterday's batching optimizer. Pushing logs.

eng-runtime-eric: ```
# sample from runtime log (streaming worker)
[2026-03-15T08:02:11Z] pool=shard-7 batch_multiplier=64 queue_len=312 cache_size=12.4GB evict_ops=1852
[2026-03-15T08:02:34Z] pool=shard-7 batch_multiplier=64 miss_ratio=0.42 mem_used=13.1GB
```

prod-ops-mike: Customer impact: a few enterprise tenants hitting timeouts on long-chat flows. CS got two tickets from Prod customers complaining about repeated reconnects. No broad data loss.

cs-lina: Confirmed — tickets INC-4872 and INC-4873 report truncation of streaming sessions and repeated reconnects. Both are mid-tier accounts; we should flag for potential credits if the incident persists >1h.

eng-ml-julia: Quick hypothesis: KV eviction threshold calculation drifted after the quantized cache refactor. Continuous-batching interacts poorly because it generates long-lived KV entries that prevent clean eviction. Risk: cascade to neighboring shards.

oncall-ryan: Tactical plan: 1) throttle continuous batching multiplier on shard-pool-7 -> set max_multiplier=8 2) roll a config hotfix to kvcache eviction window (reduce age threshold from 10m -> 3m) on canary nodes (2 nodes) 3) monitor for rollback window 20m. Who can apply the config?

eng-runtime-eric: I'll apply the multiplier throttle via runtime flags. Command: `curl -XPOST https://ops-api/flags/shard-7 -d 'max_multiplier=8'` then `kubectl rollout restart deploy/stream-worker-shard-7 -n inference`. Doing it now on canary nodes.

release-bot: Deploy started: rollout/stream-worker-shard-7-canary (2/2) -> healthy. image: runtime:v3.6.2-hotfix-20260315

eng-runtime-eric: Can confirm canary nodes show batch_multiplier capped at 8 and queue length dropped from 312 -> 28 within 45s. Memory usage dropping ~25%.

sre-amy: Recomputing metrics... P95 back to 190ms on canary; 5xx down to 1.2% for canary traffic. Rolling to rest of shard-7.

prod-ops-mike: Applying kvcache eviction window change on canary: `opsctl set kvcache.eviction.age=180s --shard shard-7 --env=canary`

eng-ml-julia: Note: hotfix reduces resident lifetime; watch for regression in hit ratio. If we overshoot we could increase external upstream calls.

oncall-ryan: Agreed. We'll do canary -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% with 5m observation. Release window started.

release-bot: Canary -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% progressed. No failed pods.

sre-amy: Metrics after full rollout: cache hit ratio stabilized at ~84% (was 58), P95 160ms, P99 760ms, 5xx back to baseline 0.6%. No observed increase in upstream calls over next 10m.

cs-lina: Customer tickets updated. Notifying impacted customers with initial summary and ETA for postmortem.

eng-runtime-eric: Root cause notes for postmortem: batching optimizer introduced a path that escalates multiplier when prefix-miss patterns occur. That path didn't account for optimized quantized KVs which added retention metadata; eviction heuristics failed to age those entries properly. Regressed in runtime:v3.6.1 -> v3.6.2.

eng-ml-julia: Addendum: long-run mitigation: revert multiplier hysteresis change and add defensive guard where batch_multiplier growth is capped based on available cache headroom. Also add circuit-breaker to fall back to smaller batches if mem pressure > 80%.

prod-ops-mike: Customer impact assessment: ~2.1k streaming sessions affected over 47 minutes, primarily increased reconnects and degraded latency. No data corruption. Recommend crediting impacted tenants per SLA >30m.

oncall-ryan: Handoff: I'm handing to @sre-amy for follow-up postmortem and rollback watch for next 6 hours. Summary posted to #postmortems and I'll include timeline. If anything spikes, page me. :thumbsup:

sre-amy: Acknowledged. I'll create the incident timeline and assign owners for metric dashboards, postmortem draft, and runtime patch.

release-bot: Hotfix tag: runtime:v3.6.2-hotfix-20260315 deployed to shard-7 and canary selectors removed.

eng-runtime-eric: Patch: PR #4621 merged (throttle fallback + eviction tuning). Will schedule a formal rollback-only test in staging later today.

cs-lina: Sent customer notifications and opened credit requests for affected accounts.

sre-amy: Incident declared resolved at 2961122950. Follow-ups: postmortem in 24h, add automated alert for unusual batch_multiplier spikes, add canary test that simulates quantized-kv retention.

oncall-ryan: Thanks team. Good triage and fast roll. Closing thread. :white_check_mark:
